title: Surgical Code Repair Protocols — compilation + tests + style (prompt pack)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working prompt pack + evaluation plan for onboarding models on our code-repair/refactor surface. Focus: small-to-medium code snippets where the model is asked to make changes that ensure compilation, add/repair unit tests, and enforce style constraints. The goal is to catch regressions that affect production codegen quality (compilation breaks, flaky tests, style violations that block CI).

Scope and assumptions:
- Languages: Python (primary), JavaScript/Node, and a small Java subset.
- Target models: candidate LLMs we run through the onboarding pipeline (open models + Redwood-verified variants).
- Execution environment: ephemeral container with language runtimes and test harness (pytest, jest, junit-lite).
- Prompts should be short and reflect real dev requests (bug fix, add tests, refactor to meet style guide).
- We expect some iterative prompt variants (concise instruction, verbose context with stack traces).

High-level categories (each category contains 40–80 prompts):
1) Compile-Fix (make the snippet compile/run)
   - broken imports, renamed symbols, missing return, type mismatch, async/await misuse
   - include scenarios where a small API surface changed upstream (function renamed)
   - measure: compiles/runs (exit 0), diff size, human-readable rationale present in reply

2) Unit-Test Synthesis & Repair
   - generate minimal unit tests for a given function signature and docstring
   - repair failing tests by modifying implementation or test (we prefer implementation fixes if task asks to fix code)
   - generate property-based tests where appropriate (Python hypothesis examples)
   - measure: tests added, tests pass in harness, coverage delta for the target function

3) Style-Constrained Refactor
   - apply style rules: PEP8 (line length, naming), consistent async usage, remove console.log in lib code, replace var with const/let, avoid deep nesting by early returns
   - enforce company lint rules (we'll map to a subset of rules in the harness)
   - measure: linter pass (flake8/eslint), before/after lint errors, reasoning clarity

Prompt structure templates (we will randomize variants):
- Minimal: "Fix the following Python function so it compiles and passes its tests:\n\n<CODE>\n\nReturn only the corrected file content and a one-line explanation."

- Contextual: "You are a senior engineer. The module below is failing CI with ImportError and a failing test. The failing test is provided. Fix the module to make the test pass. Explain your change in two short bullets at the top. Then provide the corrected file."

- Rigorous: "Refactor the function to conform to PEP8, reduce cyclomatic complexity to <= 6, and add pytest-style unit tests that cover happy-path and one edge-case. Keep public API identical."

Sample prompts and expected grader behavior (short examples):
1) Python compile-fix example:
   Prompt: "Fix and return corrected file. The test expects compute_discount to return a float. The code currently raises TypeError."
   Input snippet: def compute_discount(price, rate):
       return price * rate
   (but tests pass ints and decimals; simulated bug: missing Decimal handling)
   Grader: run pytest; require test exit 0; check that function returns float/Decimal; record token usage and time-to-fix.

2) JS style refactor example:
   Prompt: "Make this utility lib pass eslint:recommended. Avoid var, use const/let, and add a small test using jest. Return modified files only."
   Grader: run eslint; run jest; require 0 eslint errors (warnings allowed), jest pass; measure size of changes.

Scoring rubric (automated, numeric):
- Compilation/CI pass (binary): 40 points (pass full harness)
- Unit test correctness: 30 points (new tests pass + target coverage threshold met)
- Style/lint compliance: 15 points (0 errors)
- Explanation quality & traceability: 15 points (automated heuristics: presence of short rationale, mentions changed lines, one-line summary)
Notes: We also store failure modes for manual triage: hallucinated imports, removed functionality, incorrect edge-case handling.

Dataset partitions and meta tags: 
- small-fix (<= 30 LOC): many quick compile fixes, high signal for compiler errors
- test-write (10–100 LOC): functions with clear spec/docstring to base tests on
- style-refactor (10–200 LOC): functions or small modules where only style/structure changes are allowed
Each record will include simple text metadata in the harness: language, LOC, seed-id, expected-failing-assertion (if any).

Evaluation harness notes (runbook):
- Container image: redwood/eval-runtime:2026-02 with Python 3.11, Node 18, openjdk 17
- Script flow: 1) extract model response; 2) map to file(s) using simple delim heuristics (triple backticks or file headers); 3) run linter, then tests, then compile (javac) as applicable; 4) capture stdout/stderr and exit codes; 5) compute scores; 6) archive artifacts.
- Edge-case handling: if model returns prose only without code, mark as 'no-code' and score 0 for compile and tests. If model returns multiple divergent implementations, pick the first file block.

Prompt variants we must include (list for generation):
- direct fix, minimal instructions
- senior-engineer persona (encourages conservative fixes)
- aggressive refactor (allow API changes, used only in separate split)
- failing test included vs failing test NOT included
- stack trace included (simulate real CI output)

Quality checklist for prompt pack (manual):
- [ ] 50 Python compile-fix prompts ready
- [ ] 40 Python test-write prompts ready
- [ ] 30 JS style-refactor prompts ready
- [ ] 20 Java compile-and-test prompts ready
- [ ] seed annotations for randomization and split tags

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we require models to include a changelog-style header? (helps tracing)
- How strict on API-preservation for 'fix' category? Current plan: preserve public signatures unless prompt explicitly allows API changes.
- Where to surface hallucinated dependency warnings in console? (console+artifact bucket?)

Short prompt-engineering notes (observations from quick runs):
- Persona prompts ("You are a senior engineer") reduce tendency to rewrite entire modules and keep diffs smaller. Good for compile-fix category.
- Asking for "one-line explanation" increases presence of traceability, but models sometimes invent test names; grader strips test names and runs actual tests.

Example record (text form for a single prompt):
- seed: surgical-0001
- language: python
- category: compile-fix
- prompt-variant: persona-stable
- input-snippet: (see attached)
- harness-commands: "pytest -q; flake8 --exit-zero"

Acceptance criteria for onboarding a model (provisional):
- overall score >= 78 on a held-out set (balanced across categories)
- no high-severity failure modes in > 3% of prompts (hallucinated imports, silent behavior change)
- median repair time under 12s per prompt (for streaming evals)

Notes to reviewers:
- This pack is intentionally heavier on small fixes and test-write tasks than broad refactors. We want to detect regressions that directly impact CI and developer trust.
- Expect iterative additions: after first pass we'll add more edge-case tests (floating point nuance, Unicode, timezone).

Appendix: quick example prompts (copy-ready)
1) "Fix the module below so pytest passes. Keep function name compute_total unchanged. Provide only corrected module and a two-line rationale."
2) "Add two pytest tests for is_valid_email based on the docstring. Tests should cover a valid case and one invalid input."
3) "Refactor this file to meet PEP8 line length <= 88 and replace camelCase names with snake_case. Keep behavior identical. Provide changed files only."

-- end of pack draft --

Notes to self: push to git 'surgical-repair' branch, create quick PR with harness YAML and example runner. DM @Dimitri for container image update and ask SRE for ephemeral quota for larger runs.
